notes.text: The sheet is editorial working material on printed IHES letterhead. Its upper reference reads SGA 4 VII p. 20; no date or total page count is written. The bottom-left 23 is treated as the archive sheet number, not an authorial page number.
notes.basis: Observation: whole, both halves, crop 01. The archive-number classification follows the supplied conventions and packet context.

notes.text: Item a asks to add 5.6 and states that tilde X-et is localement cohérent, with an inserted algébrique, d. torsion. The next clause uses sss in its condition on the scheme X. Several inserted (ref) slots and cancellations show that the wording was being revised.
notes.basis: Observation: item a and crops 02–07. This describes the written assertions and editing state; it does not verify the mathematical claims.

notes.text: Item b starts with a filtered projective system and affine transition morphisms, writes X as its inverse limit, cites EGA framed IV 8, and gives a tilde X-et expression using baseline limtop with a left arrow underneath. The word Âlors has an actual roof mark above A.
notes.basis: Observation: half a and crops 08–10. Neither the limit theorem nor the cited reference was checked.

notes.text: The instruction En déduire pour 5.7. is readable. A small right-hand Cor. 5.6.1. has two circled additions: qu. cpt at left and resp. coh at right. The short quasi-separated abbreviation is inline, not the left circled addition. Some cancelled corollary wording remains unreadable.
notes.basis: Observation: half a and crop 11; the claimed corollary is not mathematically reconstructed.

notes.text: The lower pencil references are SGA 4 IX p. 42, note pour la p. 8, and VII 2.1 c) (p. 9), corriger. Pour and corriger are underlined, and IX/VII each have upper and lower strokes.
notes.basis: Observation: half b. H illegibility for pour and tentative erroné do not match the visible words.

notes.text: The prior C question about sss/ssi is answered separately in a and the corollary: both visible forms are sss. The prior Âlors/Alors question is resolved to Âlors. All fifteen mechanically numbered C marks have explicit outcomes.
